when: before any 1872 article was downloaded, scored or read

dataset.note: the 1859 archive used in development (faro_1859.tar.gz, sha256 3f15312a...) matches the same revision

window_rule: publication date = the YYYY-MM-DD prefix of the scan filename as parsed by bin/extract_window.py, inclusive; scans that fail to parse as JSON or lack lccn are excluded and counted; no deduplication beyond the dataset's article segmentation

base_laya.precision_rule: the 1859 MPS rule: fp32 below laya mps_amp_min_rows rows per call, autocast at or above
base_laya.order: scored once, in bin/extract_window.py article order
base_laya.revision_note: the revision 1859 actually loaded (Hugging Face main, lastModified 2026-10-03, the only snapshot in the M6 cache); laya 0.4.1 does not pin by default, so freeze/config.json (1859) named no revision and the earlier draft wrongly cited the reviewed SHA 55cf4c4e. 1872 enforces it with LAYA_REVISION and HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
base_laya.long_articles: articles over short_max_tokens (300) are scored with predict_long windows, as in 1859 (bin/laya_score.py with freeze/config.json for questions and short_max_tokens)
base_laya.verified: 2026-10-10 UTC: with LAYA_REVISION=7b928d82..., HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and bin/laya_score.py on the M6, the first 512 articles of the 1859 window scored identically (to 4 decimals) to the 1859 run
base_laya.integrity: laya verifies every listed file against these SHA-256 digests (LAYA_SHA256_DIGESTS) before any weight is parsed; a mismatch aborts the stage

ft_laya.amp: fp16 (LAYA_CUDA_AMP in the laya-batch compose template)
ft_laya.image: laya-batch:e974cca5eb42 on llm02, image ID sha256:7db9c7e879c57e8e530fc5504577aa6b2a274198b44b9b5a4ebae5169760b58f (laya 0.4.1, torch 2.14.1+rocm7.2)
ft_laya.integrity: bin/run_1872.sh checks the checkpoint's model.safetensors SHA-256 on llm02 and the image ID before scoring

systems.flag_rule: a system flags an article when its score as written to 4 decimals is >= its cutoff, or its rg pattern matches; fine-tuned Laya keeps the first 4,096 tokens of a longer article (right truncation) and such articles are counted; base Laya windows long articles as in 1859

pool.definition: union of the articles flagged by strict_rg, fuzzy_rg, base_laya and ft_laya
pool.cap_rule: no cap: every pooled article is labeled

loose_net.pattern: freeze/loose.rg via bin/rg_flags.sh, run over articles outside the pool
loose_net.n_rule: H = loose-net hits outside the pool; N = max(5, ceil(H / 400)); n = max(1, round(H / N)) articles with Python round() (half to even) when H > 0, and no net stratum when H = 0; drawn by simple random sampling without replacement with random.Random(1872); each sampled article weighs H / n
loose_net.commit_before_labeling: H, N and n (results/1872/labelset_draw.txt) and key.tsv (line numbers and weights, no text) are committed under results/1872 before any labeling starts

sonnet.harness: bin/run_agents.py: claude -p --model claude-sonnet-5-5 (full ID), isolated as in labelers.sandbox
sonnet.parse: id<TAB>YES|NO per line, validated by bin/check_labels.py

gemma.server: the same gateway as 1859 (its private URL is a local setting, local.env), a LiteLLM gateway that moved to a Kubernetes cluster after the 1859 run and is still backed by Ollama 0.34.4 (rocm) on the GPU host; OpenAI-compatible chat completions; client key read from the macOS keychain into LLM_KEY only
gemma.parse: first YES/NO word in the reply; a length stop with no answer is UNPARSED and goes to adjudication
gemma.drift_check: done 2026-10-10 UTC on 20 random 1859 items (random.Random(1872)): 18/20 match the 1859 Gemma labels on both the gateway path and direct Ollama (same 2 borderline items flip: a0690 NO->YES, a0198 YES->NO); two runs on one path agree 20/20. Disclosed as a measured run-to-run difference; Gemma disagreements go to adjudication either way

opus_adjudicator.role: settles every Sonnet/Gemma disagreement, every Gemma UNPARSED, and 30 random agreements (random.Random(1872))
opus_adjudicator.harness: bin/run_agents.py: claude -p --model claude-opus-5-5 (full ID), isolated as in labelers.sandbox
opus_adjudicator.blind: article text and prompt only, never either labeler's answer
opus_adjudicator.final_label: the adjudicator's call where it adjudicated, the consensus label elsewhere; agreed-check overturns are reported and trigger no relabeling
opus_adjudicator.batching: bin/make_batches.py at 45000 chars, from the manifest order (as in 1859)

labelers.sandbox: each agent is a fresh headless Claude Code run (claude -p, Claude Code 2.1.296, auto-update off) started in its own sandbox directory outside the repository that holds only its own batch files and prompt, launched exactly as bin/agent_outputs.agent_cmd and agent_env: --restricted (user/project/local settings, plugins and hooks ignored; file tools confined to the directory; settings files writable only by a person), --strict-mcp-config, --tools Read,Write, --permission-mode acceptEdits, --no-session-persistence, the full model ID with --model; an allowlisted environment (PATH HOME USER LOGNAME TMPDIR LANG TERM) plus CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1, and the runner refuses to start if a proxy or model-override variable is set; the resolved model and permission denials are logged per run; verified before registration by bin/smoke_agents.py (results/agent_smoke_test.md)
labelers.no_switching: no role changes model, build, host or settings after its first 1872 item; a resolved model other than the pinned full ID aborts the stage (bin/run_agents.py); if a pinned model becomes unavailable, that role restarts from its first item on a replacement named in a dated amendment
labelers.collection: bin/run_agents.py keeps an answer only from a run whose log shows exactly the pinned model and records it with its SHA-256 in SANDBOX/_verified.tsv; bin/collect_agents.py accepts a batch only from its owning agent's folder, only if that hash matches, and only if the shared validator (bin/agent_outputs.py: one line per id in order, exact column count, YES/NO) passes; anything else is a failed batch

failures: an agent whose output fails validation is re-run with a fresh agent, up to three attempts per stage run; earlier attempts are kept, an agent's first complete answers for a batch stand, and accepted answers are attested with their SHA-256; if any agent is still not done, the stage stops unlogged (bin/run_agents.py exit 3) and is re-run with ATTEMPT and REASON; a re-run restarts only agents that still owe a batch and accepts answers only for batches without an attested answer; the third (MAX_STAGE_RUNS) and any later run of an agent stage (opus_checker_run, label_run, adjudication_run) is final, and a run after the third happens only if the third stopped before finishing and is listed as a deviation; on a final run whatever is still missing goes to these rules: a Sonnet batch gets MISSING labels and goes to adjudication (kind sonnet-missing); an item whose Sonnet label is MISSING and whose adjudication is unanswered is excluded from every system and listed; a missing or UNPARSED checker verdict counts as kept; an unanswered adjudication item keeps the Sonnet label and is listed; fine-tuned scoring is re-run from the start if it fails; any re-run of a started stage needs a stated reason and keeps the earlier outputs (bin/run_1872.sh)

human_audit.who: an independent annotator recruited by the author (not the author, not an LLM); fallback: if nobody is found within 4 weeks of the 1872 labels being final, the author does it
human_audit.design: 1872: the labeled items are partitioned by priority into exactly one stratum each: S1 ft AND keyword (strict or fuzzy); S2 ft and no keyword; S3 keyword and no ft; S4 base Laya only; S5 loose-net sample. Each stratum first gets min(25, size); the rest of the 250 is allocated proportionally to (size - first share) by largest remainder; draw by random.Random(1872) within stratum (bin/draw_audit.py). 1859: 50 final-YES and 50 final-NO drawn separately with random.Random(1872)
human_audit.procedure: two blind pages (bin/make_audit_page.py --set 1872 with freeze/labeler_prompt_1872.md, --set 1859 with freeze/labeler_prompt.md): article text and the frozen prompt verbatim only, no highlighting, no labels, strata or scores in the page source; 10 hidden repeats per page; partial completion: all completed items are used, and a stratum under 80% complete is reported as incomplete; an author-fallback audit is disclosed as not blind to the key
human_audit.reporting: Cohen's kappa and raw agreement per stratum with 95% intervals; H1 and H2 recomputed with human labels substituted, as a sensitivity analysis; the LLM key decides H1 and is described as an LLM-adjudicated key
human_audit.estimator: per stratum: raw agreement (Wilson interval), Cohen's kappa, positive and negative agreement, and p1_s = share of audited LLM-YES items the human calls YES, p0_s = same for LLM-NO items; a quantity with no audited items is not estimable and its LLM label stands. Corrected H1/H2 (sensitivity): every labeled item gets y_i = p1_s or p0_s by its LLM label (net items weigh H/n); precision_k = sum over flagged of w*y / sum over flagged of w; recall_k = sum over flagged of w*y / sum over all of w*y; 2,000 bootstrap resamples of audited items within stratum, seed 1872, percentile intervals; H1's unmatched-sighting condition stays on the LLM key
human_audit.samples: 1859: results/audit/sample_1859.tsv and items_1859.jsonl, drawn and committed before any 1872 download, and redrawn byte-identically by the frozen bin/draw_audit.py (sha256 efd1b9d99057e7bf23d8fe3e6609d67094baaeab06bee9b7965cf3d064102f02); 1872: drawn by bin/run_1872.sh audit and committed under results/1872

analysis.script: bin/score_1872.py (validated before any 1872 download by reproducing the 1859 results)
analysis.unit: the article; sensitivity analysis groups pool and net articles into reprint groups (shingle_words 5, max_shingle_df 20, reprint_containment 0.5, as Freeze 1) and repeats H1 and H2 with a cluster bootstrap
analysis.post_download_code_rule: code written after download is allowed only if it is a pure function of committed stage outputs, serves a sensitivity or exploratory analysis whose choices are pinned in the pre-registration, is named in section 7, and is committed and hashed before it touches any 1872 output

drift_checks.gemma: done 2026-10-10 UTC on 20 random 1859 items (random.Random(1872)): 18/20 match the 1859 Gemma labels on both the gateway path and direct Ollama (same 2 borderline items flip: a0690 NO->YES, a0198 YES->NO); two runs on one path agree 20/20. Disclosed as a measured run-to-run difference; Gemma disagreements go to adjudication either way
drift_checks.qwen_checker: done 2026-10-10 UTC on 20 random flagged 1859 items: 20/20 match the 1859 checker run (data/finetune/drift_qwen_items.jsonl)

hypotheses.H1: primary (Freeze 1 bar), point estimates, unrounded values
hypotheses.H2: confirmatory secondary: recall(strict OR ft) - recall(strict), supported if the 95% paired stratified bootstrap lower bound > 0
hypotheses.H2_prime: secondary, not confirmatory: same with (strict OR fuzzy) as the baseline

run: every stage runs through bin/run_1872.sh STAGE with literal settings; agent prompts are rendered into ~/scratch/aurora-1872-sandbox by bin/render_agent_prompts.py; results/1872_stage_log.tsv records each output's SHA-256 and is committed after every stage
